channel.title: Doc Radar
channel.description: Upcoming documentary releases from the distributors, broadcasters, streamers and sales agents that matter. Updated weekly.

item.title: Blue Planet III
item.description: The third series of this nature documentary uses the very latest in underwater filming techniques to reveal brand new and untold stories from magical underwater worlds focusing on five major underwater habitats: the tropical seas, temperate seas, polar seas, high seas and deep seas. Venture deeper beneath the waves. David Attenborough reveals ocean life more surprising, more intelligent and more precious than we ever realised.

item.title: Don't Let The Bastards Grind You Down
item.description: Directed by Christoph Farwig. "Don't Let The Bastards Grind You Down" is a documentary film about British social policy. The focus is on the political struggle against neoliberal austerity policies, which have their origins in the hated Thatcher government. The film features the former socialist MP Dave Nellist, who is now the national chair of the Trade Unionist & Socialist Coalition and Hannah Sell, the general secretary of the Socialist Party. The film features a local election campaign in the miners' town of Nuneaton, students campaigning against an increase in tuition fees and refuse workers from Birmingham striking against massive cuts to their wages.

item.title: Allies in Exile (BBC Storyville)
item.description:
A Storyville documentary that follows Syrian film-makers Hasan Kattan and Fadi Al-Halabi. Having forged a friendship while living through, and filming, the war in Syria, they now face a very different reality as they navigate the UK asylum system.
Turning the camera on themselves, they document a new chapter in their own lives shaped by uncertainty, bureaucracy and displacement, offering a deeply personal and very raw exploration of friendship and belonging. This heart-wrenching film offers an intimate perspective on life in exile and the enduring power of storytelling in the face of adversity.

item.title: An Unknown Substance (BBC Storyville)
item.description: Vladimir Kara-Murza is a prominent Russian opposition politician and Pulitzer Prize-winning journalist who survived two near-fatal poisonings before being sentenced to 25 years in prison after speaking out against Russia’s invasion of Ukraine. This documentary short follows his wife, Evgenia Kara-Murza, during his imprisonment as she mounts a global campaign to bring him home and ensure that his voice would not be silenced.

item.title: Bradley Walsh: Out of This World
item.description: Bradley Walsh is heading Out of This World in a new series exploring some of the greatest mysteries on – and beyond – our planet. With his trademark humour, curiosity and willingness to ask the questions the rest of us are thinking, Bradley travels across Britain, Europe and America in search of answers to one enormous question: are we really alone? From UFOs and USOs to Atlantis, Stonehenge and crop circles, Bradley approaches the unexplained with an open mind, a healthy dose of scepticism and plenty of laughs.

item.title: Of Times There Were Before
item.description: Directed by Eshan Sharma. Of Times There Were Before is a portrait of Romila Thapar, one of the world’s most influential historians and public intellectuals. At ninety-four, having lived through much of the making of modern India, she stands at an unusual distance from the past she has spent a lifetime studying. The film began with a simple question: who is the person behind the historian’s name? Shot at her home in New Delhi, it is an attempt to encounter Thapar beyond the authority of her work and the public image built around it. What emerges is a portrait of a life still in conversation with its own time.

item.title: Taken: Natalee Holloway (Netflix)
item.description: Directed by Dani Sloane. Beth Holloway, Natalee's mother, tells the full, definitive story of the case that's haunted her for the past 20 years - from the day of Natalee's disappearance to the dramatic confession two decades later.

item.title: Ninho: Fame Ain’t Worth It (Netflix)
item.description: Directed by Thibaut de Longeville. At the height of his success in 2025, French rap star Ninho considers leaving music behind. This documentary looks back on the triumphs, sacrifices and personal challenges that brought him to that crossroads.

item.title: Children of Palestine
item.description: Directed by Stefano Zito. The documentary reflects on the situation in Palestine from the perspective of a journalist, an activist, and a geopolitical analyst. It offers a deeply human perspective that seeks to raise public awareness. In a world where numbers are counted every day, the director attempts here to count the names. An important message of love for Palestine and for humanity, reminding us that «we are all children of Palestine»—meaning that each of us must consider ourselves part of the same human family.

item.title: Body to Heart
item.description: Directed by Jenny Barruol. In the picturesque village of Mazan in Southern France, known for the Gisèle Pélicot rape case, three women embark on a journey to heal from domestic and sexual violence by doing horse therapy sessions.

item.title: The Courage to Stand Up
item.description: Directed by Will Glitch. Deep in the "grassroots" world of the booming British stand-up comedy scene, real performers give their unique insights of their real life stories, aspirations, and struggles - on and off stage

item.title: This is the House: If I Don’t See You, I Love You
item.description: Directed by Claudia Owusu. A Ghanaian-American father and daughter duo work through their crowded basement in search of family archives. Through intimate questions and answers, they reconcile the distance caused by immigration, divorce, and loss.

item.title: Every Grain of Dirt
item.description: Directed by Aya Chouaib. Every Grain of Dirt documents life in South Lebanon under ongoing threats of displacement and war. As sweeping evacuation orders force over a million people from their homes, some choose to remain. Among them is Ismail, a shepherd who refuses to leave his village — even as bulldozers arrive to erase it, nearly burying him alive as he stands in defiance before the machine.

item.title: Portraits of Slovak and Czech Britain
item.description: Directed by Simona Vrabcová. Transitioning from a photographic exhibition to film, this documentary captures multi-generational stories of Slovak and Czech migrants building lives and finding belonging in Britain. It highlights individuals who have impacted modern British society through personal archives and intimate conversations.

item.title: A House in One Night
item.description: Directed by Lily Tonkin-Wells. It is said that Penrhos cottage was built in one night. According to Welsh folklore, if you could build a house overnight on common land, with smoke rising from the chimney by dawn, the place would be yours to keep. 200 years later in rural Pembrokeshire, the house stands still in time. Beneath its thatched roof lived Rachel and Maria, two sisters who spent their days crafting a life that defied societal rules written for women. Quietly radical, the pair were celebrated by the whole community. Tŷ Unnos is a fairytale documentary told through the eyes of the children who once visited. Recounting memories of Penrhos and the legacy of its last owners, the past flickers back to life.

item.title: High End: The Watch Theft Ring (Netflix)
item.description: Directed by Cristóbal Valenzuela Berrios. Investigates Chile's high-profile Caso Relojes ("Watch Case") scandal, in which a suitcase full of smuggled luxury watches and jewelry unmasked an illicit underground network, connecting criminal elements to Chile's social elite.

item.title: Beyond
item.description: Directed by Ben Menashe. Follows people living with and beyond cancer as they discover strength, connection, and a new sense of possibility through climbing. Set between indoor walls and wild mountain rock, it is a powerful story about recovery becoming adventure.

item.title: Dear Henry: Our Fight for Justice
item.description: Directed by Tim Maynard. Henry Nowak’s family speak for the first time. In this documentary, they say they may have been “manipulated in their darkest hours” by both Hampshire and Isle of Wight Constabulary and the police watchdog in the months following his murder. Bodycam footage shows the officers arresting Henry as he lay dying on the ground. The family has spoken to ITV News’ UK Editor Paul Brand about the way Henry was treated and their own dealings with the police in the months after his death.

item.title: A Town Called Needville
item.description: Directed by Audrey Lane. Told through 35mm photographs and first-person narration, A TOWN CALLED NEEDVILLE traces the filmmaker's four-month inpatient stay at an all-women’s mental health facility in Needville, Texas.

item.title: The Emerald Underground
item.description: Directed by Darren Kelly. A short documentary following the stories of three independent bands from across Ireland; The Psychs, IMLÉ and Dead Assets. Each band shares their passion for music, the many struggles they face on their journey, and what keeps them going.

item.title: Fault Lines
item.description: For Noah Lane, the ocean has always been a place of freedom. But when a near-fatal accident at infamous Irish big wave spot Mullaghmore brings him face to face with his own mortality, the life he has built around the water begins to take on a different meaning.

item.title: My Friend, Kev
item.description: Directed by Colin Peppard. A filmmaker reconnects with an old friend, quietly revealing the distance time can create.

item.title: Journey to the End of the Ego
item.description: Directed by Alastair Lee. The scene is the almost mythical landscape of Ben Loyal, one of Scotland's most remote mountains towering over the Arctic Ocean. The cliff is one of the finest sweeps of clean unclimbed rock to be found anywhere in the land. The climber is the thought-provoking controversial live-wire, who goes by the name of Franco Cookson. This is the epic story of the UK's most dangerous trad route and the 105 days of climbing it took to realise one man's dream; 'Nothing is Lost' E12 7a.

item.title: Life Sure Is Sweet
item.description: Directed by Drew Coalson. Two years in the making, "Life Sure Is Sweet" is a independent coming-of-age snowboard documentary produced by the creative collective TDI (Technically Doing It). Featuring an all-Black and Brown crew of riders travelling and filming across the globe, the film moves beyond high-level action sports progression to explore deep themes of cultural identity, community, lifelong friendship, and charting your own path in the mountains.

item.title: Unprotected: Murder in Galicia (Netflix)
item.description: Directed by Jorge Laplace. Documentary film that tells the story of Isabel Fuentes. In April 2015, alleged burglars left her on the brink of death in her own home, in the village of Pazos, in Verín. From the very beginning, the Guardia Civil sergeant in charge of the case suspected that the account of what had happened did not add up and tried to protect Isabel from further attack.

item.title: Awkwafina: The Unlikely Cook (Apple Original Films)
item.description: Hollywood actor and comedian Nora Lum (a.k.a. Awkwafina) is the descendant of restaurant royalty...but she can't cook. Join the star on an inspiring culinary road trip as she learns the craft and attempts to revive her family's beloved Chinese eatery.

item.title: Making Marie Antoinette (MUBI)
item.description: Directed by Eleanor Coppola. Eleanor Coppola turns her camera on her daughter, Sofia, as she shoots Marie Antoinette. Catching every detail of the behind-the-scenes and on-set action, Eleanor captures the feat of Sofia’s directing a landmark film aged 34, and muses on what it means for a mother to watch her daughter at work.

item.title: Avedon
item.description: Directed by Ron Howard. Richard Avedon's photographs didn't just reflect culture, they shaped it, and continue to do so. The feature documentary AVEDON traces the life and legacy of an artist who used fashion, portraiture, and commercial photography to explore identity, power, fear and beauty. With unprecedented access to Avedon's archive, including never before seen photos, behind the scenes recordings, and interviews with those who knew him best, AVEDON is a visually stunning examination of the mind of an artist who shaped our collective image of the 20th century.

item.title: Finding Faith
item.description: Directed by Mary McCartney. A short film contextualising the cultural significance of George Michael's Faith album via unheard interview voice-over, unseen images by Herb Ritts, and behind-the-scenes footage of the Faith music video.

item.title: Klaus Nomi - Chanteur du troisième type (ARTE)
item.description: Directed by Thomas Boujut.

item.title: Haus Tumbuna
item.description: Directed by Matty Hannon. A socially engaged project and commissioned documentary film in Ulingan Bay, Papua New Guinea that documents the establishment of a self-sustaining, culturally specific timber surfboard factory within the local community. The project, founded by Nickolas Kirriwom and Nicholas Wynnychuk, aims to decolonize cultural impact, foster cultural revival and healing, and highlight the connection between community, culture, spirit, and the natural world through the sustainable practice of building traditional ocean-going craft.

item.title: Do You See What I See? Cinéma Fantastique Then and Now
item.description: Directed by Kat Ellinger. Exploring France's rich history of fantasy cinema, this film details the genre from it's foundation to the present.

item.title: Manhood (BBC Storyville)
item.description:
Dallas businessman Bill Moore aims to make penis enlargement as commonplace as Botox and bring the procedure into the mainstream, positioning male cosmetic surgery as a growing part of the aesthetics industry.
The documentary follows several men, including an OnlyFans creator and a father of five, as they put their bodies on the line and undergo surgery in pursuit of physical transformation.
Through intimate access to both the practitioners selling the dream and the men buying into it, the film traces the insecurities, trauma and societal pressures driving each of them, while raising uncomfortable questions about the ethics of an industry built on male self-doubt.
Filmed over two years, with dark humour and unexpected tenderness, this is a timely and revealing portrait of identity and self-image as cosmetic surgery among men continues to rise.

item.title: Jean Gabin - La guerre, c'est pas du cinéma ! (ARTE)
item.description: Directed by Patrick Jeudy.

item.title: Magic in the Mundane
item.description: Directed by Leigh Brooks. A cinematic journey into the overlooked miracles of everyday existence.

item.title: Whispers in the Woods
item.description: Directed by Vincent Munier. In the heart of the tranquil Vosges forests, where lynxes, bears and deer roam freely, Vincent Munier accompanies his father on his expeditions. He not only seeks to capture the visual wonders of this forest kingdom, but also aims to make its sounds audible. Every whisper of the forest is a reminder of the knowledge of nature that his father once imbued in him – knowledge that Vincent now passes on to his own son. Vincent Munier combines breathtaking footage of nature and its sounds to create a fairytale-like cinematic experience that slows time down.

item.title: Nuisance Bear
item.description: Directed by Gabriela Osio Vanden. A polar bear is forced to navigate a human world of tourists, wildlife officers, and hunters as its ancient migration collides with modern life. When a sacred predator is branded a nuisance, it becomes unclear who truly belongs in this shared landscape.

item.title: A Fox Under a Pink Moon
item.description: Directed by Mehrdad Oskouei. At just 16, Soraya is already creating stunning drawings and sculptures that are as beautiful as they are dark. This strong-willed Afghan sculptor and illustrator has been trying for five years to escape Iran and join her mother in Austria.

item.title: Whiddy (ARTE)
item.description: Directed by Adrian McCarthy. A small rural community in Ireland welcomes in a major, global oil company with open arms but just 10 years and numerous oil spills later, that dream turns into an unimaginable nightmare. 50 lives lost in a tragedy that silenced and divided the community and still haunts it to this day.

item.title: 1 in 2
item.description: Directed by David Wilkinson. Nearly one in two of us will be diagnosed with cancer at some point in our lives. David Nicholas Wilkinson is one of them, twice over. 1 in 2 follows Wilkinson through his own treatment, where he discovers a steep rise in bowel cancer among people far too young to be screened for it, and far too young, it seems, to be believed.

item.title: Flhorrida 2: Even Flhorrider
item.description: Directed by Phil Rankin. In 2017, a horrid holiday happened... Now, in 2025, a holiday happened horridly... again! SmellBad Films present, a rubbish sequel no one in the universe asked for. But this time, it will be... EPIC!

item.title: Answering The Call
item.description: Directed by Martin Danneels. On Ireland’s rugged west coast, a rare call cuts through the summer night: a corncrake has returned. For those who have grown up with its rasping cry, this is more than the return of a bird. It is the sound of home, of childhood summers and a living connection to a landscape shaped by generations. But that familiar voice is disappearing, and with it, a piece of who these communities are. In Answering the Call, communities of farmers, locals and naturalists unite in a race to save what few corncrake remain. As the community rallies to answer the call, one question becomes impossible to ignore: if they fail to act now, will they be the last generation to hear this extraordinary sound?

item.title: Women and War (ARTE)
item.description: Directed by Elwira Niewiera. In a chalet in the Ukrainian mountains, four women attend therapy sessions to recover from their very different, deeply traumatic experiences of the war. They each try, in their own way, to resume their former lives.

item.title: The Neighbourhood is Changing
item.description: Documentary on the making and legacy of Mulberry Street featuring new interviews with cast and crew

item.title: The Last Spy (BBC Storyville)
item.description: A Storyville documentary that shines a light on the extraordinary life of CIA officer Peter Sichel, who fled Nazi Germany and became one of the most influential figures in US intelligence.

item.title: When a Witness Recants (HBO Documentary Films)
item.description: Directed by Dawn Porter. In 1983, author Ta-Nehisi Coates learned that a 14-year-old boy was murdered in his Baltimore middle school. Upon revisiting the case, he uncovers the truth: Three innocent teenagers were wrongfully convicted and spent 36 years in prison — creating a lasting impact on the accused, the witnesses, and their community.

item.title: Trade Secret
item.description: Directed by Abraham Joffe. Three unlikely allies are on a mission to protect polar bears from international commercial trade. Filmed over six years across 13 countries, the film exposes the sanctioned sale of hundreds of polar bears each year on the global market. But as the investigation deepens, it uncovers a disturbing truth: those entrusted with safeguarding the species may be entangled in their continued commercialisation. The film raises urgent questions about how we protect vulnerable wildlife in a world where the lines between protection and exploitation have become blurred.

item.title: Women & the Wind
item.description: Directed by Alizé Jireh. Shot over the course of 30 days at sea, filmmaker Alizé Jireh documents the group’s voyage across the North Atlantic—from moments of stillness and calm to the chaos of storms and setbacks. With an observational approach and an eye for the emotional and physical rhythms of life at sea, Jireh captures not just the external landscape, but the internal shifts that come with navigating the vast unknown.

item.title: Observer
item.description: Directed by Ian Cheney. Filmmaker Ian Cheney embarks on an experiment in which he brings a series of keen-eyed observers - scientists, artists, a hunter - to a range of locations around the world, often without telling them where they are going, and asks them simply to describe what they see. What unfolds is a deep exploration and celebration of the power of observation: what happens when you find new ways to sense and perceive the world around you?

item.title: Nininbaori
item.description: Directed by Mathieu Achermann. Follows three para-climbers through fragments of their daily lives, where ordinary domestic gestures intertwine with the quiet precision of athletic practice. Moving seamlessly from one to the next, the film refuses hierarchy, unfolding instead like the pages of a single book written by multiple hands.

item.title: À bord du vide
item.description: Directed by Thomas Guerrin. A poetic exploration of the art of steep skiing with Aurélien Lardy. This film celebrates the art of the movement, the commitment, and the intimate relationship between the man and the mountain, and what draws us to vertical places.

item.title: My Ride or Die
item.description: Directed by Charlotte Percle. Morgan McGlashon (professional mountain guide) and Caite Zeliff (professional skier) picked obscure paths. Those paths collided and became intertwined. When their careers took off they found themselves spending less time in the mountains together but they always dreamed of one day coming back together on a proper adventure. On a 10-day expedition in Alaska, the two reconnect.

item.title: The Search for Milliseconds
item.description: Directed by Darcy Wittenburg. Inside mountain bike downhill phenom Jackson Goldstone's high-stakes bid to become one of the youngest riders in history to claim the UCI DH Elite overall title. From pre-season testing to the tense, pressure-filled moments leading into the last race of the year, the film follows Jackson and the team that supports him as they hunt for every possible edge in a sport where the smallest fractions of time can define a champion. With the title on the line and only one decisive run remaining, Jackson prepares to risk everything for the win.

item.title: Still Rider
item.description: Directed by Daniel Stark. After a mountain bike crash resulted in a life altering injury, Chantelle Grafton and her husband Warren have gone to great lengths to get Chantelle back out on the trails. Still Rider explores this journey, highlighting the unanticipated complexities that come with a major spinal cord injury and more importantly the benefits of prioritising adaptive design for those with and without accessibility issues.

item.title: My Grandmother’s Sketchbook: Under Mont Blanc
item.description: Directed by Max Romey. A 30-year-old sketchbook leads Max Romey to the Mont Blanc region. The Alaska-based watercolor artist and environmental advocate sets out to follow in the footsteps of his grandmother, who visited this landscape in the late 1990s and captured it in dozens of drawings. With mountain guide Hillary Gerardi, Max attempts to locate each sketch’s exact origin point. Many match perfectly—until the Mer de Glace throws him off course. The glacier has changed too much in 30 years to recognize.

item.title: Too Old Not To
item.description: Directed by Clementine Bourke. “Feel the fear and do it anyway” is the motto that 55-year-old Heli Murray teaches, and practices, as a birth doula and endurance athlete. Parallel to navigating motherhood, divorce, menopause and grandmotherhood, the ocean has been Heli’s sanctuary and outlet for expanding her own edges.

item.title: Robson
item.description: Directed by Philip Forsey. Two of the world’s most accomplished ski mountaineers, Christina Lustenberger and Guillaume Pierrel, have carved their names into history with bold first descents across the globe. Now, turning their sights on Mount Robson, the highest and most formidable peak in the Canadian Rockies, they retrace the steps of pioneering alpinists who came before them, pushing the line between past and present. Battling towering walls of ice, snow and rock, unpredictable weather, and the weight of a dream that has challenged generations, their journey becomes as much about resilience and legacy as it is about the pursuit of a descent few have ever dared to imagine.

item.title: Good Luck, Kid
item.description: Directed by Renan Öztürk. Grit, gear, growth – this film is a portrait of Taylor Shaffer’s coming-of-age as a photographer and filmmaker, following his creative trajectory as he shepherds Alex Honnold and Tommy Caldwell through a 2,500-mile expedition to attempt a single-day traverse of the Devil’s Thumb massif and finds his artistic voice amid risk, friendship, and a changing Alaskan landscape.

item.title: It Takes Two To Tandem
item.description: Directed by Cat Aeppel. Longtime riding partners Sam and Jazz take a tandem bike across some of their favourite trails in the Rockies, marking ten years since their first tandem adventure together. Part celebration, part reflection, the film explores friendship, trust, and the rare joy of moving through the world in sync.

item.title: The TransAtlantic Way
item.description: Directed by Fergus Coyle. At dawn, riders set off from Cork City on a self-supported journey of up to 2,400km, bound for the finish line across Derry’s Peace Bridge, battling fierce winds, rugged terrain, and shifting light. Narrated by veteran long-distance cyclist and event organiser Adrian O’Sullivan, the film immerses viewers in Ireland’s dark and mystical landscape, capturing the endurance, solitude, and raw beauty of the western coast.

item.title: The Himalayas in My Heart
item.description: Directed by Jérémy Bigé. In 1802, the Survey of India Institute launched the Great Trigonometrical Survey, a colossal undertaking aimed at precisely mapping British India from which the world became aware of the vast scale of the Himalayan range. From August to November 2024, using these historical maps, Jérémy Bigé makes his way on foot over 2,300km from Indian Kashmir to central Nepal. His goal: to connect the various Himalayan cultures in a single journey by following routes from the past.

item.title: Back By Tea Time
item.description: Directed by Tom Hill. In a world where it feels like we have everything we could ever want at our fingertips – Amazon, Spotify, next-day delivery, door-to-door, Uber, Netflix, Deliveroo, quicker than ever before, pure convenience and luxury without a second thought – in that world, perhaps there is something to be said for choosing the long way round. When Alice Lemkes realises she's out of milk, it is an excuse for an adventure in ‘Scotland's Last Great Wilderness.’

item.title: More than Everest: The Life of T.H. Somervell
item.description: Directed by Simon Pierse. T. Howard Somervell (1890-1975) is best known for his role in the 1922 and 1924 expeditions to climb Everest. This film explores the lesser known aspects of Somervell's remarkable life as a missionary surgeon, artist and composer of music.

item.title: SUSTRAIAK, Lost Roots
item.description: Directed by Luis Arrieta Etxeberria. This is the story of Hiba, Bachir and Manan. Three young people who migrated from their countries as children and arrived in Navarre without any adult with them and alone. Here they have discovered climbing and the mountains, but their paths will gradually begin to diverge.

item.title: Kidical Mass
item.description: Directed by Isaac Seigel-Boettner. After years of exploring their world by bicycle, the Moss family knew that they wanted to raise their kids on two wheels. But after a frightening accident on the way to school, they had to take a step back from their pedal-powered ambitions. Then they found Kidical Mass. This is the story of how one family is helping to reclaim their streets, one giant kid bike party at a time.

item.title: You Can See Everything
item.description: Directed by Nathan Fielder. Thirty-four days before she's sent to prison, notorious Silicon Valley founder Elizabeth Holmes invites a skeptical film crew to document her every move. What begins as an intimate portrait of an enigmatic felon becomes a mind-bending three-year journey into the abyss.

item.title: Time and Water (National Geographic Documentary Films)
item.description: Directed by Sara Dosa. Facing the death of his country’s glaciers and the loss of his beloved grandparents, Icelandic writer Andri Snær Magnason turns his archives into a time capsule to hold what is slipping away — family, memory, time, and water.

item.title: To Hold a Mountain
item.description: Directed by Biljana Tutorov. In the remote highlands of Montenegro, a shepherd mother and daughter proudly defend their ancestral mountain from the threat of becoming a NATO military training ground, stirring memories of the violence that shattered their family.

item.title: American Doctor
item.description: Directed by Poh Si Teng. United by a shared oath to save lives, three American doctors—Palestinian, Jewish, and Zoroastrian—work in a besieged hospital in Gaza in the middle of a genocide comitted by Israel, and return to the United States to fight for the patients and colleagues they left behind.

item.title: Tin Castle
item.description: Directed by Alexander Murphy. Along a long-forgotten road, the O’Reillys live in a rundown trailer stranded in the middle of the fields. Pa’, Lisa, and their ten children weather the seasons in their tin castle, heirs to a way of life on borrowed time. Under threat of eviction, their tenuous balance falters, yet – steadfast in their tradition – they resist. The children laugh, the dogs bark, the trailer holds on – but for how long?

item.title: Zahir
item.description: Directed by Julien Nadiras. When Katherine Choong suggested to her friend Éline Le Menestrel that they tackle the Zahir, a classic route in the Swiss Alps and a demanding gem of the Wendenstöcke, Éline agreed... on one condition: that they only use sustainable transport to get to the foot of the wall. As the days passed suspended on the rock, they realized the scale of the challenge: intense commitment, tiny holds, accumulated fatigue from cycling... every movement became a challenge. Between motivation and euphoria, perseverance and doubt, would Katherine and Éline manage to reach their Zahir, that summit where audacity and wild beauty come together?

item.title: Obsession: The Beryl Burton Story
item.description: Directed by Stuart Pollitt. A documentary about Britain’s greatest athlete. Undefeated for 25 years, Leeds-born amateur cyclist Beryl Burton won seven World Championships, beat men’s records and transformed women’s sport; all while working on a Yorkshire rhubarb farm. Through unseen archive, letters and intimate interviews, the film explores the glory of her achievements and the cost of her obsession, particularly on her relationship with her daughter Denise, who followed her into competitive cycling.

item.title: Inside the Mountain
item.description: Directed by Jack Homan. In 1988, Paul Eastwood and his climbing partner became the first men to free-climb Britain's deepest open cave shaft, rising from within the UK's largest underground chamber and traversing around its highest unbroken waterfall, three times the height of Niagara falls. The iconic route will have gone unrepeated for almost 40 years. Decades later a new team of climbers, Olympian Molly Thompson-Smith and legend Steve McClure, will tackle the climb once again, hoping to join the few who have ever free-climbed the route.

item.title: 75 Seconds
item.description: Directed by Marco Tribelhorn. On a foggy March evening in Norway, freeskier Jacob Wester triggers an avalanche and is swept off a cliff. For 75 seconds, he fights for his life inside a roaring mass of snow, while his wife Sofia waits in silence below. This is an account of chaos, fear, and hope inside an avalanche.

item.title: Big Jim: An American on Everest
item.description: Directed by Jim Aikman. “Big Jim” Whittaker (1929-2026) was a legendary Pacific Northwest mountaineer who became the first American to summit Mount Everest on May 1, 1963. This short documentary explores his “brotherhood of the rope” with his twin brother, Lou, as well as Nawang Gombu Sherpa, his Everest climbing partner and lifelong friend. Featuring rarely seen 16mm footage from the 1963 Everest Expedition, archival images from the Whittaker family collection, and interviews filmed in Jim’s late 80s, the film is both an intimate portrait of an extraordinary life and a celebration of the adventurous spirit that helped define a generation of climbers.

item.title: Glacier's Requiem
item.description: Directed by Saddiq Abubakar. In isolation on Iceland’s Snæfellsnes Peninsula, Nigerian-born modular synthesis artist Colloboh transforms glacial and oceanic recordings into sonic compositions; uncovering a dialogue between ice and sea that reshapes his understanding of consciousness, ecological collapse, and humanity’s place within both.

item.title: Framed
item.description: Directed by Bernardo Giménez. Siebe Vanhee sets out to onsight Voie Petit, a brutal 12-pitch 8a+ line at 3,500m on the Grand Capucin, completely alone - no partner, no static ropes, just lead rope-solo technique and a drone circling above. But even a solo mission as a professional climber has a crew: a manager on the phone, a sponsor waiting for footage, a director on the glacier, and Vanhee himself playing climber, cameraman and storyteller all at once, selfie-interviewing his own exhaustion pitch by pitch.

item.title: The Hillbilly Scientist
item.description: Directed by Paul Mellor. While modern running has evolved toward sleek curation, optimisation, and commercialisation, Lazarus Lake has spent 50 years designing formats with an unapologetic, honest difficulty. The Hillbilly Scientist reveals that Laz’s cruellest courses are rooted in a deeply scientific understanding of human psychology and physical limits. This is the only official documentary dedicated to the creator of the Barkley Marathons and Big’s Backyard Ultra. Filmed over more than a year, it reveals the man behind the myth through never-before-seen footage, exclusive testimonials, and exceptional access to Laz’s world.

item.title: Rongo
item.description: Directed by Finlay Woods. With plenty of powder to go around, un-ridden waves rolling into secret golden beaches, and local characters to greet you with a smile, six professional athletes make the most of every moment during an action-packed adventure through Aotearoa, NZ!

item.title: Same Sun - Cycling through Africa
item.description: Directed by Fabienne Engel. The story of Wiebke Lühmann's journey from Freiburg to the Cape of Good Hope. Honest, raw, and close to the inner and outer challenges of a 430-day bicycle trip. Her journey takes her through 22 countries, Sahara storms, the rain season, the Congo Basin, and the deserts of Namibia. What begins as a search for independence becomes an intimate exploration of identity.

item.title: Aldo's Raptor Roundup
item.description: Directed by Neil Losin. Six-year old Aldo spends an exciting weekend banding migrating raptors in Cape May, New Jersey with his friend John, a volunteer bander with the Cape May Raptor Banding Project.

item.title: The Last of the Lookouts
item.description: Directed by Ryan Wilkes. High atop Sinkut Mountain in northern British Columbia, Bart Vanderlinde begins each summer's day the way he has for the past nine years: scanning the forest for smoke. He's among the last lookout people in the province. Where three hundred lookouts once formed an interconnected network across the region, Bart now often keeps watch alone. This is an intimate portrait of a man and a profession facing obsolescence. The film gives insight into the craft of fire detection while capturing the quiet solitude of a life lived in observation.

item.title: Beura
item.description: Directed by Gregor D. Sinclair. The tale of the Cailleach Bheur, the Celtic goddess of nature, storms and winter, is well known to many in the Gàidhealtachd. Said to have carved the mountains and glens with ice, and borne the islands like children on her back, the Cailleach disappeared long ago leaving us only with her song – a sad, cautionary tale. This Gaelic arts project brings music, film and verse together to reimagine Cailleach’s story for the modern era.

item.title: A Mystical Ornithology
item.description: Directed by Jeremy Seifert. Immersed in the songs of blue jays, yellow-throated warblers, and red-shouldered hawks on his forty-six-acre farm in rural South Carolina, acclaimed poet and ornithologist J. Drew Lanham exchanges calls with the birds that stop over at his home during their seasonal migrations. For Drew, these creatures are gods, transcendent beings who summon a response of reverence. Reverberating with sound, music, light, and ethereal cinematic expression, A Mystical Ornithology weaves a kinetic texture for the senses and invites you into a poetic evocation of the paradox of love and grief within the changing nature of the seasons.

item.title: Borrowed from the Earth
item.description: Directed by Zach Johaneson. Tells the story of the powerful connection between the Blackfeet people and horses, and how that life-giving relationship remains alive today. Throughout their histories, both horse and Indigenous people have been corralled - horses by fences, and Indigenous people onto reservations. Yet centuries-long attempts to subdue both ultimately strengthened the bond between them. Saddle up for a visually poetic journey from the origin story of the horse to the modern day Indian Relay Race. Filmed on the Blackfeet Reservation in Browning, Montana.

item.title: SILA
item.description: Directed by Ciril Jazbec. Set on an island 600 kilometers north of the Arctic Circle, this intimate vérité portrait follows two young Inuit coming of age. Created in close collaboration with a local children’s home and filmed in the Greenlandic language, the story traces identity, tradition, loss, and resilience. Living alongside its protagonists, the film observes a fragile passage between deep cultural roots and an uncertain, rapidly changing world.

item.title: Secret Rivers of the Nakanai
item.description: Directed by Alexandre Lopez. In the village of Ruraï, in Papua New Guinea, people tell of a water hidden deep within the Nakanai Mountains so pure that anyone who drinks it is said to gain extraordinary powers. Immersed in the heart of a tropical rainforest, a team of cavers including the inimitable Cédric Lachat, set out to uncover this mysterious underground river system.

item.title: Teeth to the Wind
item.description: Directed by Ben Knight. Before Michael Gardner's death in Nepal in 2024, he and his climbing partner Sam Hennessey had started a film project about their friendship. Remarkable alpinists, but reluctant filmmakers, Teeth to the Wind realizes Gardner and Hennessey's original vision: a joyful and unassuming glimpse at what they referred to as “the spirit.”

item.title: Blank Patterns
item.description: Directed by Alexi Godbout. A collection of athlete portraits following Jacob Bélanger, Emma Patterson, and Ugo Troubat. Through their individual stories, the film explores the experiences, choices, and communities that shaped the lives they lead today. While each has taken a different path, together they reflect the many ways people find their place within skiing and contribute to the culture in their own way.

item.title: Ripple
item.description: Directed by Ryder Schwartz. Two women sit by the lake that raised them and have a conversation about what it means to be a freeride skier. After dedicating their lives to the sport, they question the meaning of it all. More than anything, this is a story about surrendering to the present moment. A story about being water.

item.title: Ridgeline
item.description: Directed by Anna Brannon. Professional musician and composer Liz Derstine heads into the wilderness to chase a very different goal: attempting a self-supported Fastest Known Time on the Pacific Crest Trail.

item.title: Casey
item.description: Directed by Erica Gianesini. Casey is a young woman on a journey of self-empowerment, shaped by community and a fierce love for skateboarding. This short film is a tribute to trans+ joy and the spaces that allow people to be unapologetically themselves. Made in collaboration with Transkaters and Not A Phase charity.

item.title: Zuma Rock
item.description: Directed by Luke Logan-Malik. Rotimi, an amateur climber and writer from London with deep family roots in Nigeria sets out to achieve the unthinkable: a first ascent of Zuma Rock, a 300m monolith considered sacred by the communities who live in its shadow. To do it, he enlists Olympic climbing champion Shauna Coxsey but neither of them has ever tackled a wall of this scale.

item.title: Searching for SuperCrust: The Lost Tapes
item.description: Directed by Chris Burkard. Five cyclists set out to cross Europe's largest glacier by bike. An expedition 30 years in the making, the film explores the past, present, and future of Vatnajökull through the stories of those who have braved the glacier’s icy expanse on two wheels.

item.title: Wild Ice
item.description: Directed by Mike Schwartz. As winter slowly reveals itself across the Canadian Rockies, artist and skater Elladj Baldé and photographer Paul Zizka chase the season’s first wild ice - a journey that becomes a reflection on freedom, connection, and the human desire to move through life with intention.

item.title: The Rare Folk 2
item.description: Directed by Joe Barnes. Follow up to The Rare Folk

item.title: Rodeo On Ice
item.description: Directed by Lindsey Hagen. With skijoring poised to become a potential addition to the 2030 Winter Olympics, lifelong equestrian Britta Nancarrow assembles a team to push her skijoring to the next level. The film follows Nancarrow as she trains with skier Mike King and snowboarder Sandra Hillen, taking their on-snow skills to their very first competition.

item.title: The Kelp Collector
item.description: Directed by Jack Breedon. After a career in science, Sandy Webb has found a new passion in retirement: collecting and cataloguing the diverse algae species that inhabit the waters near her Melbourne home. With the precision of a scientist and the eye of an artist, she transforms her discoveries into exquisite pressed-seaweed specimens, The kelp collector reveals how Sandy's dedication to documenting local marine life connects her to the coastal environment she calls home.

item.title: The Art of Hold Shaping
item.description: Directed by Dean Tucker. An intimate documentary exploring the world of Dan Yagmin as the creative force behind Decoy Holds. Moving between wild landscapes, workshop processes and climbing walls, the film is a portrait of an artist shaping not just holds, but the way we experience climbing itself.

item.title: Marcus & Me
item.description: Directed by Dominic Gill. As a participant in the Outdoor Inclusion Coalition, 'little' Marcus explores the less-known corners of his Pittsburgh back yard to seek out opportunities for climbing and connection with nature.
